title: Uniform witness normalization: eliminating existential search from verifier acceptance
claim: Establishes a general deterministic normalization principle for Boolean certificate verifiers: existential acceptance is equivalent to running the verifier on the canonical zero witness. The theorem turns unbounded certificate search into a single verifier call for every input under the UniformNormalization interface, providing a reusable route from nondeterministic verification to deterministic decision.
novelty: Introduces a verifier-level witness-erasure interface and proves a uniform search-elimination theorem across all natural-number encoded verifiers. Unlike the ledger's CNF-specific locality and certificate-checking results, this theorem works before any formula encoding is chosen and isolates a general mechanism suitable for polynomial verifier pipelines.

prior_art.relationship: The public ledger contains CNF assignment locality, resolution soundness, and finite truth-table certificates. None presents this verifier-level normalization interface.

research_direction: Deterministic normalization of nondeterministic certificate verification toward P equals NP

provenance.discovery_basis: Inspected the five records returned by the native public ledger on 2026-11-23, including their precise claims and formal statements. No listed theorem states this abstract canonical-witness equivalence. This comparison is limited to the project ledger and is not a comprehensive external literature search.

evidence.reproduce: Run the pinned open-agent check research/submissions/witness-normalization.json --lean in the isolated full-Lean environment.

attribution.contributions: Designed the abstract verifier interface, formalized its canonical-witness theorem, and prepared this submission using an AI assistant.

limitations: The theorem is parametric in the UniformNormalization interface. Encoding-specific normalization instances and a concrete cost model are follow-up integration work. It does not by itself state the canonical full P-versus-NP theorem.
